task: Build the dependency foundation that makes every Finding-system write exactly-once and every mutable runtime witness cryptographically bound and freshness-checkable.
outcome: Terminal output shows: Finding ledger integrity: PASS — 100 concurrent appends produced 100 unique durable rows, replay returned the original IDs, and a stale CAS wrote zero records. Runtime evidence integrity: PASS — the signed receipt matches the current source, command, environment, toolchain and artifact bytes; tampered, stale, non-authoritative or unstable receipts are refused with a reason code.
facts: B-1fa6 accepted docs/requirements/decisions/dynamic-finding-system-execution-plan.md as the design and acceptance truth source.
Section 9.3 requires internal order 3A ledger integrity before 3B runtime evidence integrity.
Current finding_add serializes a read-push-write section, but allocates display IDs from array length and has no general FindingLedgerReceipt or idempotency/CAS transaction.
StoryStore atomic replacement validates temp JSON then renames it, but does not currently expose a schema-neutral fenced multi-record transaction or acknowledged file and directory fsync boundary.

Current VerificationExecutionReceipt records exit/output/selector/time data but does not implement the accepted RuntimeEvidenceReceipt artifact, source, environment, toolchain, trust and content-addressed blob bindings.
B-03b7 depends on this Story for identity and lineage persistence; B-e6d9 depends on both for applicability enforcement.
constraints: Audit and reuse existing per-Story, main/B-META, process-event, build and Store transaction primitives instead of creating an uncoordinated lock tree.
Persistence authority proves exact durable bytes only and must never promote candidate, route, baseline, historical or receipt records into semantic gate authority.
The supported fault model is canonical shared local filesystem plus crash, kill, retry, stale lock and partial temp writes; unsupported multi-host/NFS and corruption assumptions must fail closed.
FindingLedgerReceipt and RuntimeEvidenceReceipt fields, signatures and exact-byte CAS behavior must match the accepted document.
Legacy Finding bytes remain readable and are not rewritten merely to backfill ledger identity.
Story 3 must not import or implement Story 2 identity/lineage policy or Story 1 applicability/routing/gate policy.
All process facts consumed by lifecycle or future gates require registry plus mechanical verifier updates and adversarial mutation tests.
